title: Malta Year 8 Math — LCM & HCF Practice
question: 8 questions: LCM & HCF Practice.
intro:
**8 questions:** 4 with two numbers (find HCF and LCM), then 4 with three numbers (find LCM).

- Every starting number in the two-number questions is below 50.
- In a common-factor ladder, divide only when a prime divides **every** entry.
- The product on the left is the **HCF**.
- For two numbers, multiply the left factors and the bottom entries to get the **LCM**.
- For three numbers, check that no two bottom entries share a factor before multiplying them; otherwise find the LCM of the bottom row first.

questions.title: HCF and LCM of 12 and 20
questions.prompt:
Use a common-factor ladder for **12 and 20**.

Choose the row giving **both** the HCF and the LCM.
questions.solution:
- Divide only by a prime that divides **every** number in the row.
- Stop when no prime divides them all.

\[
\begin{array}{r|rr}
2 & 12 & 20 \\ 2 & 6 & 10 \\  & 3 & 5
\end{array}
\]

**HCF: multiply the common factors on the left.**

\[
\operatorname{HCF}=2\times2
\]

\[
\operatorname{HCF}=\boxed{4}
\]

**LCM: left factors × bottom entries.** No two bottom entries share a factor greater than 1.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}=2\times2\times3\times5
\]

\[
\operatorname{LCM}=\boxed{60}
\]

**Check:**

\[
4\times60=240
\]

\[
12\times20=240
\]

- **Avoid the trap:** multiplying the two starting numbers counts their common factors twice.
- The HCF and LCM columns also have different meanings.

questions.title: LCM of 9, 15, 21
questions.prompt:
Use a common-factor ladder to find the LCM of **9, 15, 21**.

Show your ladder on paper, then enter the LCM.
questions.solution:
- Divide only by a prime that divides **every** number in the row.
- Stop when no prime divides them all.

\[
\begin{array}{r|rrr}
3 & 9 & 15 & 21 \\  & 3 & 5 & 7
\end{array}
\]

**HCF: multiply the common factors on the left.**

\[
\operatorname{HCF}=3
\]

\[
\operatorname{HCF}=\boxed{3}
\]

**LCM: left factors × bottom entries.** No two bottom entries share a factor greater than 1.

\[
\operatorname{LCM}=3\times3\times5\times7
\]

\[
\operatorname{LCM}=\boxed{315}
\]

- **Avoid the trap:** the left-hand product is the HCF.
- The LCM also needs the bottom entries.
- Here no two bottom entries share a factor greater than 1.

- Divide only by a prime that divides **every** number in the row.
- Stop when no prime divides them all.

\[
\begin{array}{r|rrr}

\end{array}
\]

**HCF: multiply the common factors on the left.**

\[
\operatorname{HCF}=7
\]

\[

\]

takeaway:
- HCF: left factors only.
- LCM: left product times the LCM of the bottom row; for coprime bottom entries, multiply them.
